options: Original data that has been masked so that some fields are hidden
A new dataset generated by computer simulation, containing fake data with the right properties or attributes
A backup copy of production data stored in a separate region
Data that has been swapped between rows to hide identities
Aggregated data that no longer shows individual records
questions.explanation: Synthetic data is generated using computer simulations; it is fake data that carries the right properties or attributes of the real thing without containing it.

questions.stem: What drawback do techniques such as data generalisation, swapping, masking and encryption share?
options: They can only be applied to structured data
They are too slow for large datasets
They all change the original data, which most people do not want
They require a separate licence
They cannot be reversed
questions.explanation: All these privacy techniques alter the original data, which is not desired by most; synthetic data avoids this by generating a separate dataset.

questions.stem: In the customer-information example, what do synthetic data tools produce?
options: An encrypted copy of the real customer table
A sample of real customers with their names removed
A list of customers who have consented to sharing
A dummy customer dataset with name, email, contact number and family details unrelated to the originals
An aggregated count of customers by region
questions.explanation: Synthetic tools create dummy customers with realistic fields such as name, email and contact number, but nothing related to the original data.

questions.stem: Who benefits from synthetic customer data, according to *I Am Datapedia!*?
options: Developers building data pipelines and data scientists building models, without breaching regulatory or compliance clauses
Auditors who need to see the original records
Customers who want to check their own details
Marketing teams who need real contact numbers
Attackers who need realistic targets
questions.explanation: With synthetic data, developers can build pipelines and data scientists can build models without worrying about breaching regulatory or compliance clauses.

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT listed as a use of synthetic data?
options: Generating a larger dataset from a small one for analytics
Fulfilling compliance requirements to anonymise data
Sharing a representation of production data with the QA team for testing
Parking fake data somewhere to confuse attackers
Replacing the production database permanently
questions.explanation: Synthetic data supports machine learning, scaled-up analytics, compliance, QA testing and decoys for attackers; it does not replace production data.

questions.stem: For which discipline is synthetic data described as 'the best fit'?
options: Financial auditing
Machine Learning
Network security
Master Data Management
Project management
questions.explanation: Synthetic data is described as the best fit for Machine Learning.

options: Only the confidential fields of the original data are replaced
Original data combined with other synthetic data to generate a further set
The whole set of data is replaced with reference to the original
The original data left intact but encrypted
A random sample of the original data
questions.explanation: In Full Synthetic Data, the entire dataset is replaced, using the original only as a reference for its properties.

options: Only confidential data is replaced
The whole dataset is replaced
Half of the rows are deleted
Data is generated from two synthetic sources
Data is masked rather than generated
questions.explanation: In the partial approach, only the confidential data elements are replaced with synthetic values.

questions.stem: Which type of synthetic data is said to provide the most privacy capability?
options: Full Synthetic Data
Partial Synthetic Data
Masked Data
Hybrid Synthetic Data
Generalised Data
questions.explanation: Hybrid Synthetic Data, which refers to original as well as other synthetic data to generate another set, provides the most privacy capability.

questions.stem: Which analytics scenario does *I Am Datapedia!* give as an example of using synthetic data to enlarge a small dataset?
options: Detecting duplicate customer records
Calculating the average age of customers
Encrypting transactions before archiving
Counting distinct product categories
Predicting the outcome if the number of similar transactions increased by 500%
questions.explanation: Synthetic data can generate a larger dataset from a small one, for instance to predict what happens if similar transactions increase by 500%.
